item.title: Draft Radio Act ordinance amendment: 800 MHz station registration and consultation results
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications published consultation results and a Radio Regulatory Council response on 2026-11-06 concerning a draft Ministerial Ordinance amending the Regulations for Enforcement of the Radio Act. The proposal would enable portable stations for 800 MHz broadband low-power wireless systems to be established as registered stations, adding a reference in Article 17, item 12 to the technical standards in Article 49-37 of the Radio Equipment Regulations. The ministry states that technical standards covering frequencies, antenna power and sharing with other radio systems were already established through amendments dated 2026-07-30. The consultation ran from 2026-09-12 to 2026-10-16 and received submissions from 10 respondents; the ministry also identified a correction to the draft's technical-standard reference following comments. The draft provides for commencement on promulgation, but the supplied excerpts do not establish a promulgation date or the substance of the council's response. Original title: 電波法施行規則の一部を改正する省令案に係る意見募集の結果及び電波監理審議会からの答申 Public Comment Results Published | Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) | Published 2026-11-06 | First detected 2026-11-07 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation. item.title: Digital Agency publishes explainer on administrative RAG apps in Government AI Gennai
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-06, the Digital Agency announced an explanatory video on administrative retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) apps in Government AI Gennai; this is an informational announcement, not a regulatory amendment. The apps reference registered manuals, guidelines and reports to answer questions and organize, analyze, compare or summarize information. Examples include an EASY electronic administrative document management system Q&A app, which may not be available in every ministry or agency, and a document-management Q&A app for internal Digital Agency use. The explanation warns that AI answers may contain errors or omissions and calls for checking original sources, particularly dates, document numbers and numerical values, and observing each ministry or agency's rules on information permitted in Gennai. The Agency also describes development on request for apps expected to be used across multiple ministries or agencies, with completed apps generally published on Gennai.
